Küresel bir etki üretmek isteyen herkesi bekliyoruz!
summary:
Satellites in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) rely on static ground-based Conjunction Data Messages (CDMs) that fail during geomagnetic storms. As seen in the February 2022 Starlink loss and the May 2024 G5 Superstorm, sudden solar-driven thermospheric expansion increases atmospheric drag by up to 800%, shifting satellite positions by tens of kilometers while ionospheric blackouts sever ground communication.

AEGIS-LEO solves this critical vulnerability by moving space weather physics and collision avoidance directly onto the spacecraft’s flight computer. Developed by Team AYAZ, AEGIS-LEO combines multi-model thermospheric physics (Jacchia-77, NRLMSISE-00), Foster 2D B-plane collision probability, an INT8-quantized Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) executing in under 150 microseconds, and a 9-agent Byzantine Fault-Tolerant (BFT) onboard swarm intelligence architecture. When a solar storm triggers unmodeled orbital decay and blackout, AEGIS-LEO autonomously synthesizes fuel-optimal Vis-Viva and Sequential Convex Programming (SCP) micro-burns, reducing delta-v propellant consumption by up to 88% while strictly enforcing NASA-STD-8719.14B and FCC 5-Year deorbit compliance.
details:
### 1. What Does AEGIS-LEO Do and How Does It Work?

AEGIS-LEO (Autonomous Edge-AI & Physics-Informed Orbital Safety Shield) is a full-stack autonomous flight software and mission control platform designed to protect Low Earth Orbit (LEO, 160–2,000 km) satellites from the compounded threats of geomagnetic storms and orbital debris (Kessler Syndrome).

During severe solar storms (G4/G5), coronal mass ejections heat the upper atmosphere, causing sudden thermospheric density surges that invalidate static ground-based collision predictions while simultaneously causing polar cap absorption (PCA) radio blackouts. AEGIS-LEO operates autonomously onboard the spacecraft through an 11-stage deterministic pipeline:

1. Space Weather & Multi-Model Thermosphere Engine: Ingests NOAA SWPC / NASA OMNIWeb Kp and F10.7 solar flux indices to compute real-time atmospheric density and along-track orbital drift across Jacchia-77, NRLMSISE-00, and Exponential scale-height models, coupled with Cowell RK4 numerical propagation (J2, Solar Radiation Pressure, and Battin third-body Sun/Moon perturbations).

2. Adaptive Debris & Drag Risk Index (A-DRI) & Foster B-Plane: Computes 2D Gauss-Legendre B-plane collision probability (Foster 1992 / Chan 1997) and fuses it with thermospheric drag uncertainty, NASA ORDEM debris flux, and propellant feasibility into a unified 0.0–1.0 A-DRI score.

3. Sub-Millisecond INT8 Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) & MPC: Executes an onboard PyTorch PINN (<150 microseconds latency, <10 KB memory) protected by Triple Modular Redundancy (TMR) against South Atlantic Anomaly (SAA) Single-Event Upsets (bit-flips). Synthesizes proactive Vis-Viva micro-phasing and Sequential Convex Programming (SCP/MPC) avoidance trajectories.

4. 9-Agent Byzantine Fault-Tolerant (BFT) Swarm Intelligence: Nine specialized onboard agents (SolarStorm, Thermosphere, Risk, Astrodynamics, EdgeInference, Constellation ISL, ComplianceWatchdog with absolute VETO power, ReentryDisposal, and MissionCommander) vote asynchronously and issue SHA-256 / Post-Quantum ML-KEM (CCSDS 355.0-B-2 SDLS) signed maneuver directives.

5. 6-DOF ADCS, 5-Node Thermal & Active Debris Removal (ADR): Verifies quaternion reaction-wheel pyramid slew-to-burn readiness, 5-node orbital thermal equilibrium, RF/Optical ground station link budgets, dual-cone eclipse battery Depth-of-Discharge (DoD), Electrodynamic Tether (EDT) / pulsed laser ablation (LODR), and Universal-Variable Lambert multi-debris ADR tours.

### 2. Benefits and Intended Impact

- Prevents Catastrophic Satellite Losses: Eliminates the "ground blackout blind spot" during severe solar storms, preventing events like the February 2022 Starlink loss (38 satellites lost to storm drag).

- Up to 88% Propellant Savings: Proactive micro-phasing burns (0.325 m/s) executed hours before Time of Closest Approach (TCA) replace late reactive burns (2.80 m/s), extending spacecraft operational lifetimes by years.

- Enforces Space Sustainability by Design: Built-in auditing for NASA-STD-8719.14B (Section 4 ODAR generation), IADC guidelines, FCC 5-Year post-mission disposal rules, and Point Nemo (SPOUA) controlled reentry dispersion ellipses.

### 3. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

- Languages & Core Stack: Python 3.12, NumPy, SciPy, PyTorch 2.2+ (INT8 Dynamic Quantization & Physics-Informed Loss), SGP4.

- Backend & Mission Control UI: FastAPI (45+ REST API endpoints), Streamlit (15-tab interactive Mission Control HUD), Three.js (WebGL 3D orbital & conjunction visualizer), Plotly.

- DevOps & Verification: Docker, Docker Compose, GitHub Actions CI/CD, Pytest (385/385 automated unit and integration tests passing at 100%).

### 4. How Is AEGIS-LEO Creative & What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

- Creativity: Instead of treating space weather, orbital mechanics, attitude/thermal control, cybersecurity, and AI as isolated silos, AEGIS-LEO unifies them into a single physics-informed, radiation-tolerant onboard brain with a 9-agent BFT voting parliament where the NASA Compliance Watchdog holds an absolute safety veto.

- Factors Considered: We accounted for harsh flight computer constraints (<10 KB model footprint, SEU radiation bit-flips in the South Atlantic Anomaly), communication blackouts, propellant passivation reserves (>= 2.0 kg), quantum-era telecommand spoofing (ML-KEM lattice cryptography), and international interoperability (CCSDS 508.0-B-1 CDM XML/KVN, OEM/OPM, and NASA ODAR).

### 5. Disclosure of Super Intelligence (SI) Tool Usage

In accordance with NASA Space Apps Challenge guidelines, Team AYAZ discloses that Super Intelligence (SI) / Large Language Model coding assistants and image generation tools were used to accelerate software scaffolding, unit test authoring, documentation refinement, and conceptual UI banner illustrations (all generated visuals in the `assets/` directory include visible disclosure). All astrodynamic equations, physical constants, and verification tests were validated against standard aerospace literature (Vallado, Foster 1992, NASA-STD-8719.14B).
